subject: [PATCH] kernfs: don't hold kernfs_rwsem across notification delivery

reviews.author: Christian Brauner
reviews.summary: Applied the patch to a branch in the vfs tree and encouraged reviewers to provide Acked-bys and Reviewed-bys. Also noted that commit hashes may change due to rebase or trailer updates.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, 09 Sep 2026 21:54:06 -0700, Shakeel Butt wrote:
> kernfs: don't hold kernfs_rwsem across notification delivery

Applied to the vfs-7.4.kernfs branch of the vfs/vfs.git tree.
Patches in the vfs-7.4.kernfs branch should appear in linux-next soon.

Please report any outstanding bugs that were missed during review in a
new review to the original patch series allowing us to drop it.

It's encouraged to provide Acked-bys and Reviewed-bys even though the
patch has now been applied. If possible patch trailers will be updated.

Note that commit hashes shown below are subject to change due to rebase,
trailer updates or similar. If in doubt, please check the listed branch.

tree:   https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/vfs/vfs.git
branch: vfs-7.4.kernfs

[1/1] kernfs: don't hold kernfs_rwsem across notification delivery
      https://git.kernel.org/vfs/vfs/c/23985e2b1f31

2026-09-17.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in the kernfs subsystem where a stalled worker can block all future readers of kernfs_node::name, leading to system daemons being stuck for long periods of time. The fix involves sampling the name once before the loop and dropping the lock on kernfs_rwsem, while still maintaining the reference count with kernfs_supers_rwsem.
